summary: Navigate a metre-authored museum using supplied walkable polygons and teleport targets while treating device bounded-floor geometry, authored collision and local-floor fallback as separate contracts.
objective: Navigate a metre-authored museum using supplied walkable polygons and teleport targets while treating device bounded-floor geometry, authored collision and local-floor fallback as separate contracts.
intent_signals: Teleport through a museum at correct world scale with a desktop equivalent.
example_prompts: Build a metre-scale museum with bounded-floor-aware teleport, explicit floor fallback and equivalent desktop exhibit navigation.
not_for: Evacuation, accessibility or physical-space safety certification.

entities.name: Metre-scale gallery
entities.guidance: Blender authors walls, exhibits, collision proxies and teleport anchors in metres with stable IDs; glTF preserves asset scale, not XR reference spaces.

entities.name: Walkable registry
entities.guidance: Store supplied authored walkable polygons and clearance class independently from device bounded-floor bounds; teleport targets pass authored walkability/collision only. Device bounds may drive a separate physical play-area overlay/guard.

entities.name: Locomotion router
entities.guidance: Offer direct room/exhibit controls on desktop and a declared fade/instant teleport in immersive mode; continuous motion is optional rather than assumed.

state_contract.model: Request immersive-vr through knowledge.webxr-delivery-boundary. Prefer bounded-floor when enabled, but treat its device-supplied bounds only as physical play-area metadata. Validate every teleport destination solely against the authored walkable polygon/collision registry. If room-scale physical movement is visualized or guarded, evaluate the tracked viewer position against current device bounds in that reference-space frame as a separate status; never compare virtual destination coordinates to those bounds. If bounded-floor is unavailable, request local-floor only when declared; if that fails, any emulated floor offset is labeled authored calibration and never inferred. Teleport changes the application rig within the selected reference space, never the reference-space transform itself.
state_contract.authority: Blender/glTF owns metre-scale gallery geometry, colliders and target anchors. The user agent owns reference-space poses/bounds. Three.js/WebXR owns session/reference-space lifecycle, target validation, rig offset, fade state, controller loss and desktop-equivalent selection/reset.
actions: Enter XR through the existing capability lifecycle.
Choose room/exhibit through equivalent desktop controls.
Recenter/reset application rig without rewriting source geometry.

invariants: glTF asset scale is one metre per authored metre.
Device bounded-floor bounds never replace authored walkability/collision and are never used to accept or reject a virtual teleport destination.
A rejected/unknown target produces no rig move.
Fallback floor origin and calibration status remain visible.
motion_guidance: Teleport uses a short authored fade or immediate cut with no hidden continuous acceleration; playback of the transition is presentation, not evidence of comfort for a device/user.
creative_affordances: Use floor reticles, destination silhouettes and exhibit landmarks with shape/labels as well as color.
known_limits: No headset, browser, floor calibration, comfort study, physical clearance, render or runtime was tested.

claims.statement: WebXR defines local, local-floor and bounded-floor reference-space types; bounded-floor exposes device-defined boundary geometry, while requesting a reference space can reject when the type is unsupported.
claims.scope: WebXR Device API Candidate Recommendation Draft 9 June 2026; device bounds do not certify application-authored walkability or accessibility.

object_craft.structure: Blender models gallery/exhibits/collision proxies at metre scale and exports named target anchors via glTF; no session, bounds or floor calibration is baked.
object_craft.material: Valid, blocked and unavailable destinations use distinct reticle shape and text; fade plane is runtime-only.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js validates teleport targets only against authored geometry, optionally displays device play-area status separately, and moves only an application rig.

physical_contract.scope: Application-rig teleport among validated authored targets; no physical-space or comfort certification.
state: device play-area bounds and tracked-viewer status if supplied
contact: Collision proxy validation is authored application logic, independent of device bounds.
checks: Reject target outside authored walkability/collision without consulting device bounds.
When enabled, device-bounds status evaluates only tracked physical movement in its own reference-space frame.
Bounded-floor absence follows declared local-floor/desktop path.
Reset restores rig and selection exactly.
